study: Where does the pipelined core's critical path come from, and can it be shortened without changing behaviour?
part: xck26-sfvc784-2LV-c, synthesis-only estimate at a 3.5 ns target

baseline.reading: EX performed forwarding, the address adder, alignment checks, the exception priority chain and a 32-bit tval select, all in one cycle.

attempts.change: Classify load/store misalignment and select tval at MEM, from fields already in the EX/MEM register. Only fetch misalignment, which needs the branch decision, stays in EX as a single bit.
attempts.new_critical_path: ex_mem_q.dec.imm (CSR address) -> csr legality decode -> trap_taken -> stall_mem -> ex_mem_q.mem_addr, 13 levels

attempts.change: Gate the memory request on the MEM exception alone instead of trap_taken, taking the CSR address decode off the stall path. Behaviourally identical: a CSR instruction is never a load or store.
attempts.new_critical_path: ex_mem_q.dec.is_csr -> forwarding -> EX branch compare -> redirect -> fetch buffer enables, 11 levels
attempts.reading: Removed the path it targeted, but synthesis restructured the design and a different path got longer. Net loss, reverted.

verification: Both variants: smoke PASS, hello.c MATCH against Spike at 0/1/2/4 wait states with cycle counts unchanged (484/506/590/805), riscv-tests 54/58 with only the four documented gaps.
caveat: A 2.3% gain is within the range synthesis heuristics can move on their own; these are post-synthesis estimates, not placed-and-routed results. The next real target is the redirect path from the EX branch compare into the fetch unit.
